en.heading: 24 March: one discovery and a century of tuberculosis research
en.origin: World Tuberculosis Day recalls 24 March 1882, when Robert Koch announced the discovery of the bacterium responsible for tuberculosis. WHO's historical campaign evaluation identifies 1982 as the establishment year of the day, marking the centenary of the discovery. The modern date reminds the public that tuberculosis remains an infectious disease requiring accessible diagnosis, treatment and public-health support. Koch's nineteenth-century scientific announcement is a milestone, but not the founding decision for the modern awareness campaign. The WHO sources support the 1982 centenary and its calendar rationale without naming a single modern individual who proposed the commemorative campaign.

en.purpose: Increase awareness of tuberculosis prevention, diagnosis and treatment and support efforts to reduce illness and deaths.

L'annuncio scientifico dell'Ottocento è un fatto fondamentale, ma non coincide con l'atto che ha creato la campagna moderna. Le fonti OMS sostengono la cronologia del centenario e la scelta della data, senza identificare una sola persona che abbia proposto originariamente la ricorrenza.

en.heading: 28 July: recalling the scientist behind hepatitis B discovery
en.origin: The World Health Organization recognizes 28 July as World Hepatitis Day, a date selected because it is the birthday of Baruch Blumberg, the scientist associated with the discovery of the hepatitis B virus and the development of diagnostic work and a vaccine. WHO's historical evaluation identifies 2010 as the formal institutional establishment year, although awareness efforts preceded that recognition. The modern campaign encourages testing, prevention, vaccination where applicable and access to treatment for different forms of viral hepatitis. The exact first independently documented annual celebration following WHO recognition is not established by the primary materials reviewed here and is left unknown.

en.heading: 19 April: Brazil changes the legal name of an older observance
en.origin: Brazil enacted Law No. 14,402 on 8 July 2022, establishing 19 April as Dia dos Povos Indígenas and repealing the earlier Decree-Law No. 5,540 of 2 June 1943. The new name replaced the earlier Dia do Índio formulation and recognized that Brazil contains diverse indigenous peoples with their own histories and identities. The 2022 law did not invent the 19 April calendar tradition: the earlier official date had been used since the 1943 decree. Nor does the statutory year determine when indigenous peoples began advocating for their rights. The first observance under the newly worded 2022 law is not established independently in this source and remains unasserted.

La legge del 2022 non inventò la tradizione del 19 aprile: il precedente giorno ufficiale era già previsto nel 1943. Neppure l'anno della legge coincide con l'inizio delle rivendicazioni dei popoli indigeni. La prima celebrazione specificamente organizzata sotto la nuova formulazione legislativa non è documentata separatamente nel testo e rimane non accertata.

en.heading: 15 February: Canada remembers the first maple-leaf flag raising
en.origin: On 15 February 1996 Prime Minister Jean Chrétien issued a declaration designating the annual National Flag of Canada Day. The date marks the first ceremonial raising, at noon on 15 February 1965, of the new red-and-white maple-leaf flag on Parliament Hill. The national flag itself had been approved and proclaimed earlier, in 1964–65, before the commemorative day was created three decades later. The original Canadian declaration stresses values including freedom, peace and mutual respect. It is therefore important not to mistake the adoption of the flag in 1965 for the founding of the annual observance in 1996.
en.promoter: Prime Minister Jean Chrétien issued the original 1996 declaration; the design and adoption of the flag came through separate earlier national processes.

it.heading: 15 febbraio: il Canada ricorda il primo alzabandiera della foglia d'acero
it.origin: Il 15 febbraio 1996 il primo ministro Jean Chrétien firmò una dichiarazione che istituiva la Giornata nazionale della bandiera canadese. La data ricorda il primo alzabandiera cerimoniale della nuova bandiera rossa e bianca con foglia d'acero, avvenuto a mezzogiorno il 15 febbraio 1965 sulla collina del Parlamento. La bandiera nazionale era stata approvata e proclamata nel 1964–65, oltre trent'anni prima dell'istituzione della giornata commemorativa. La dichiarazione canadese richiama valori come libertà, pace e rispetto reciproco. Non bisogna quindi confondere l'adozione della bandiera nel 1965 con la nascita della celebrazione annuale nel 1996.

it.purpose: Far conoscere la storia della bandiera canadese e il suo ruolo di simbolo civico condiviso da comunità differenti.

es.origin: El 15 de febrero de 1996, el primer ministro Jean Chrétien proclamó el Día de la Bandera Nacional de Canadá. La elección del emblema había pasado por debates y decisiones parlamentarias en 1964 y una proclamación real en enero de 1965. Es fundamental separar su adopción en 1965 del nacimiento de la jornada anual en 1996. La declaración asocia la bandera con la libertad, la paz, el respeto, la justicia y la tolerancia.

fr.heading: 15 février : le premier lever du drapeau à la feuille d'érable
fr.origin: Le 15 février 1996, le premier ministre Jean Chrétien a proclamé le Jour du drapeau national du Canada. Cette date rappelle le premier lever officiel du drapeau rouge et blanc à la feuille d'érable, à midi le 15 février 1965 sur la Colline du Parlement. Le choix du drapeau avait donné lieu à des débats et à des décisions parlementaires en 1964, puis à une proclamation royale en janvier 1965. Il faut donc distinguer l'adoption du symbole, en 1965, de l'instauration de sa commémoration annuelle, en 1996. La déclaration rappelle les valeurs de liberté, de paix, de respect, de justice et de tolérance.

de.heading: 15. Februar: Erinnerung an das erste Hissen der Ahornblattflagge
de.origin: Am 15. Februar 1996 erklärte Premierminister Jean Chrétien den Tag der kanadischen Nationalflagge zum jährlichen Gedenktag. Er erinnert an das erste feierliche Hissen der rot-weißen Ahornblattflagge am 15. Februar 1965 um zwölf Uhr auf dem Parliament Hill. Der Wahl der Flagge waren politische Beratungen 1964 und eine königliche Proklamation im Januar 1965 vorausgegangen. Die Einführung der Flagge 1965 und die Begründung des jährlichen Gedenktages 1996 sind daher verschiedene Ereignisse. Die Erklärung verbindet das nationale Symbol mit Freiheit, Frieden, Respekt, Gerechtigkeit und Toleranz.

pt.heading: 15 de fevereiro: o primeiro hasteamento da bandeira da folha de ácer
pt.origin: Em 15 de fevereiro de 1996, o primeiro-ministro Jean Chrétien proclamou o Dia da Bandeira Nacional do Canadá. A data recorda o primeiro hasteamento cerimonial da bandeira vermelha e branca com a folha de ácer, ao meio-dia de 15 de fevereiro de 1965, na Colina do Parlamento. A adoção do símbolo nacional resultou de debates e decisões parlamentares em 1964 e de uma proclamação real em janeiro de 1965. Portanto, a adoção da bandeira em 1965 não deve ser confundida com a criação do dia comemorativo em 1996. A declaração associa a bandeira à liberdade, à paz, ao respeito, à justiça e à tolerância.

en.heading: 30 September: a national day for truth, survivors and reconciliation
en.origin: Canada inaugurated the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation on 30 September 2021. The federal observance aligned with the earlier Orange Shirt Day tradition, which honoured Indigenous survivors of residential schools and the children who never returned home. The modern statutory day must be distinguished from decades of advocacy and remembrance by First Nations, Inuit and Métis communities. Canadian government sources describe the schools as institutions that removed children from families and communities under colonial assimilation policies, causing damage whose consequences remain today. The day calls for reflection, education and concrete commitment to reconciliation rather than treating one public holiday as a complete remedy.
en.promoter: Canada's federal government introduced the formal annual observance in 2021, drawing on pre-existing Orange Shirt Day and Indigenous community advocacy.
en.purpose: Honour residential-school survivors and affected families, improve historical education and support Indigenous-led reconciliation.
facts: The federal National Day for Truth and Reconciliation began on 30 September 2021.
The observance coincides with the older Orange Shirt Day tradition.
The commemoration addresses the continuing impacts of Canada's residential-school system.

it.heading: 30 settembre: una giornata nazionale di verità e riconciliazione
it.origin: Il Canada inaugurò il 30 settembre 2021 la Giornata nazionale per la verità e la riconciliazione. La celebrazione federale si sovrappone alla precedente tradizione dell'Orange Shirt Day, dedicata alle persone indigene sopravvissute alle scuole residenziali e ai bambini che non tornarono a casa. La nuova ricorrenza ufficiale va distinta da decenni di memoria e mobilitazione di comunità First Nations, Inuit e Métis. Le fonti governative spiegano che quelle scuole separarono bambini da famiglie e comunità nell'ambito di politiche coloniali di assimilazione, con conseguenze ancora presenti. La giornata invita a riflessione, istruzione e impegni concreti, senza trattare una festa pubblica come soluzione completa.
it.promoter: Il governo federale canadese introdusse formalmente la giornata nel 2021, riprendendo l'Orange Shirt Day e l'azione delle comunità indigene.
it.purpose: Ricordare i sopravvissuti alle scuole residenziali e le famiglie, diffondere conoscenza storica e sostenere una riconciliazione guidata dalle comunità.
facts: La prima ricorrenza federale si svolse il 30 settembre 2021.
Il calendario coincide con la precedente tradizione dell'Orange Shirt Day.
La giornata affronta gli effetti tuttora presenti delle scuole residenziali.

es.heading: 30 de septiembre: verdad, supervivientes y reconciliación
es.origin: Canadá celebró por primera vez el Día Nacional de la Verdad y la Reconciliación el 30 de septiembre de 2021. La conmemoración federal coincide con el anterior Día de la Camiseta Naranja, dedicado a recordar a los menores indígenas que nunca regresaron de los internados y a quienes sobrevivieron. El nuevo día oficial responde también al llamamiento a la acción 80 de la Comisión de la Verdad y la Reconciliación. Durante décadas, el sistema de escuelas residenciales separó a niñas y niños de sus familias y comunidades de las Primeras Naciones, los inuit y los métis. La jornada promueve la memoria, la educación y las medidas sostenidas de reconciliación; no supone que una festividad resuelva ese legado.
es.promoter: El Estado federal formalizó la jornada en 2021 tras la reivindicación de comunidades indígenas y la tradición del Día de la Camiseta Naranja.
es.purpose: Honrar a las personas supervivientes, a sus familias y a los niños fallecidos, y apoyar la reconciliación impulsada por los pueblos indígenas.
facts: La primera jornada federal tuvo lugar el 30 de septiembre de 2021.
La fecha coincide con el Día de la Camiseta Naranja, celebrado anteriormente.
La Comisión de la Verdad y la Reconciliación pidió una conmemoración nacional en su llamamiento 80.

fr.heading: 30 septembre : vérité, survivants et réconciliation
fr.origin: Le Canada a célébré pour la première fois la Journée nationale de la vérité et de la réconciliation le 30 septembre 2021. Cette commémoration fédérale coïncide avec la Journée du chandail orange, une initiative antérieure honorant les survivants des pensionnats autochtones et les enfants qui ne sont jamais rentrés chez eux. La nouvelle journée répond également à l'appel à l'action 80 de la Commission de vérité et réconciliation. Le système des pensionnats a séparé de nombreux enfants des Premières Nations, inuits et métis de leurs familles et communautés, dans le cadre de politiques coloniales d'assimilation. Cette date invite à apprendre, à se souvenir et à soutenir durablement la réconciliation; elle ne suffit pas, à elle seule, à réparer ces torts.
fr.promoter: Le gouvernement fédéral a instauré la journée en 2021, à la suite des mobilisations autochtones et de la Journée du chandail orange.
fr.purpose: Honorer les survivants et leurs proches, les enfants disparus et les démarches de réconciliation portées par les communautés.
facts: La première célébration fédérale date du 30 septembre 2021.
Cette date est celle de la Journée du chandail orange.
L'appel à l'action 80 demandait une commémoration nationale.

de.heading: 30. September: Wahrheit, Überlebende und Versöhnung
de.origin: Kanada beging den Nationalen Tag für Wahrheit und Versöhnung erstmals am 30. September 2021. Der bundesweite Gedenktag knüpft an den älteren Orange Shirt Day an, der an Überlebende der Internatsschulen für indigene Kinder und an diejenigen erinnert, die nie zurückkehrten. Er greift außerdem Handlungsaufforderung 80 der Wahrheits- und Versöhnungskommission auf. Im System der sogenannten Residential Schools wurden Kinder der First Nations, Inuit und Métis im Rahmen kolonialer Assimilationspolitik von ihren Familien und Gemeinschaften getrennt. Der Tag steht für Erinnerung, historisches Lernen und langfristige Schritte zur Versöhnung; ein einzelner Feiertag kann das fortdauernde Unrecht nicht beheben.
de.promoter: Die Bundesregierung richtete den formellen Gedenktag 2021 ein; indigene Initiativen und der Orange Shirt Day gingen ihm voraus.
de.purpose: Überlebende, Familien und verstorbene Kinder würdigen sowie indigene Versöhnungsarbeit unterstützen.
facts: Die erste bundesweite Begehung fand am 30. September 2021 statt.
Das Datum fällt mit dem älteren Orange Shirt Day zusammen.
Handlungsaufforderung 80 verlangte einen nationalen Gedenktag.

pt.heading: 30 de setembro: verdade, sobreviventes e reconciliação
pt.origin: O Canadá assinalou pela primeira vez o Dia Nacional da Verdade e Reconciliação em 30 de setembro de 2021. A comemoração federal coincide com o anterior Dia da Camisola Laranja, dedicado aos sobreviventes das escolas residenciais para crianças indígenas e à memória das crianças que nunca regressaram a casa. A nova data também responde ao Apelo à Ação 80 da Comissão da Verdade e Reconciliação. Durante décadas, estas escolas afastaram crianças das Primeiras Nações, inuit e métis das suas famílias e comunidades, no âmbito de políticas coloniais de assimilação. O dia incentiva a reflexão, o ensino da história e o compromisso continuado com a reconciliação, sem sugerir que um feriado resolva sozinho as consequências desse passado.
pt.promoter: O governo federal formalizou a data em 2021, após a mobilização indígena e a tradição do Dia da Camisola Laranja.
pt.purpose: Honrar os sobreviventes, as famílias e as crianças que morreram, promovendo a reconciliação liderada pelas comunidades indígenas.
facts: A primeira comemoração federal ocorreu em 30 de setembro de 2021.
A data coincide com o anterior Dia da Camisola Laranja.
O Apelo à Ação 80 pedia uma comemoração nacional.

en.heading: 8 May: Spain's exiles enter the democratic memory law
en.origin: Article 8 of Spain's Law 20/2022 of 19 October established 8 May as the annual day of remembrance and tribute to men and women who experienced exile because of the military coup, Civil War and dictatorship. The law's explanatory memorandum explicitly connects 8 May with victory in Europe over fascism and Nazism and acknowledges exiles' role in that struggle. This modern legal decision is distinct from the events of the 1930s and 1940s and from the separately established 31 October day for all victims. The act establishes the annual date but does not individually prove a first commemorative ceremony after its adoption, which remains unknown.
en.promoter: Spain's Parliament enacted Law 20/2022; Article 8 establishes the exile-remembrance day, while Article 7 creates a separate victims' day.
en.purpose: Recognize people forced into exile and preserve the history of democratic resistance, displacement and repression.
facts: Article 8 of Law 20/2022 designates 8 May as the annual date.
The law's explanatory memorandum links it to victory over European fascism in 1945.
Article 7 separately designates 31 October for remembrance of all victims.

it.heading: 8 maggio: l'esilio spagnolo entra nella legge sulla memoria democratica
it.origin: L'articolo 8 della legge spagnola 20/2022 del 19 ottobre istituì l'8 maggio come giornata annuale in memoria e omaggio alle donne e agli uomini costretti all'esilio a causa del colpo di Stato militare, della guerra civile e della dittatura. Il preambolo lega esplicitamente l'8 maggio alla vittoria europea sul fascismo e sul nazismo e riconosce il contributo delle persone esiliate a quella lotta. La decisione moderna va distinta dagli eventi degli anni Trenta e Quaranta e dalla separata giornata del 31 ottobre dedicata a tutte le vittime. La legge stabilisce la data annuale, ma non documenta una prima singola cerimonia successiva all'adozione, che resta non accertata.
it.promoter: Il Parlamento spagnolo approvò la legge 20/2022; l'articolo 8 istituisce la ricorrenza per l'esilio e l'articolo 7 una distinta giornata delle vittime.
it.purpose: Riconoscere le persone costrette all'esilio e conservarne la storia di resistenza democratica, migrazione forzata e repressione.
facts: L'articolo 8 della legge 20/2022 fissa la ricorrenza dell'8 maggio.
Il preambolo collega la data alla vittoria in Europa sul fascismo del 1945.
L'articolo 7 stabilisce separatamente il 31 ottobre come giorno per tutte le vittime.

en.heading: 19 May: Brazilian physicists receive a national day in law
en.origin: Brazil's Federal Law No. 14,769 was signed on 22 December 2023 and established 19 May as National Physicist Day throughout the country. Its articles add the date to the official national calendar, distinguishing the legal recognition of a profession from the much older history of physics and scientific research. The law names the day and its annual date but does not by itself establish why 19 May, rather than any other day, was selected. It also does not record a first national ceremony after adoption, so no inaugural year is asserted. The day provides an opportunity to discuss research, education, laboratories and the work of physicists in medicine, industry and daily technology.
en.promoter: Brazil's National Congress enacted the law, signed by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in December 2023; no single original date proposer is proven by its operative articles.
en.purpose: Recognize the contribution of physicists and support scientific education, research and public understanding of science.
facts: Law 14,769 was signed on 22 December 2023.
The law establishes 19 May as National Physicist Day across Brazil.
The day was added to the official national calendar by the statute.

it.heading: 19 maggio: il Brasile riconosce per legge la Giornata dei fisici
it.origin: La legge federale brasiliana n. 14.769, firmata il 22 dicembre 2023, istituì il 19 maggio come Giornata nazionale del fisico in tutto il Paese. Gli articoli inseriscono la data nel calendario ufficiale, distinguendo il riconoscimento giuridico della professione dalla storia molto più antica della fisica e della ricerca scientifica. La legge indica la ricorrenza annuale ma non spiega da sola perché sia stato scelto il 19 maggio invece di un altro giorno. Non documenta neppure la prima cerimonia nazionale successiva all'adozione, perciò non viene inventato un anno inaugurale. La giornata consente di parlare di ricerca, istruzione, laboratori e contributo dei fisici a medicina, industria e tecnologie quotidiane.
it.promoter: Il Congresso nazionale brasiliano approvò la norma firmata dal presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva nel dicembre 2023; gli articoli non provano il singolo ideatore della data.
it.purpose: Riconoscere il contributo dei fisici e sostenere educazione scientifica, ricerca e comprensione pubblica della scienza.
facts: La legge 14.769 fu firmata il 22 dicembre 2023.
Istituì il 19 maggio come giornata nazionale dei fisici in Brasile.
La ricorrenza entrò nel calendario ufficiale nazionale mediante la legge.

en.heading: 23 April: Spanish joins the UN's six language days
en.origin: In 2010 the United Nations Department of Public Information, later renamed the Department of Global Communications, began a programme of six language days to foster equal treatment of the UN's official languages. Spanish Language Day falls on 23 April, a date associated with the death of Miguel de Cervantes, a landmark of Spanish literature. The UN's own 2010 Spanish-language observance page records the first programme rather than requiring an invented General Assembly proclamation. The celebration is as much about language access and multilingual diplomacy as it is about literary heritage. It should not be confused with a state law creating a worldwide public holiday.
en.promoter: The UN Department of Public Information initiated the six-day programme in 2010; Cervantes is commemorated, not its modern founder.
en.purpose: Explain the role of Spanish and the other five official languages in international communication, access to information and cultural understanding.
facts: The language-days initiative was launched by the UN information department in 2010.
The date 23 April commemorates Miguel de Cervantes.
Spanish shares this calendar date with the UN English Language Day.

it.heading: 23 aprile: lo spagnolo entra nelle sei giornate linguistiche ONU
it.origin: Nel 2010 il Dipartimento dell'informazione pubblica dell'ONU, poi rinominato Dipartimento della comunicazione globale, avviò le giornate dedicate alle sei lingue ufficiali delle Nazioni Unite. Per lo spagnolo fu scelto il 23 aprile, data tradizionalmente legata alla morte di Miguel de Cervantes, autore fondamentale della letteratura in lingua spagnola. Il sito istituzionale conserva già una pagina della celebrazione del 2010: non occorre attribuire l'istituzione a una risoluzione dell'Assemblea generale che non è stata identificata. Il significato non è solo letterario: traduzione, interpretariato e accesso multilingue permettono di partecipare al dialogo internazionale.
it.promoter: Il Dipartimento dell'informazione pubblica ONU lanciò il programma nel 2010; Cervantes è il personaggio ricordato, non il promotore moderno.
it.purpose: Valorizzare lo spagnolo e il multilinguismo come strumenti di cultura, diplomazia e accesso equo alle informazioni.
facts: Le giornate delle sei lingue ufficiali iniziarono per iniziativa del dipartimento ONU nel 2010.
Il 23 aprile ricorda la figura letteraria di Miguel de Cervantes.
Lo spagnolo condivide questa data con la Giornata ONU della lingua inglese.

en.heading: 20 September: university sport becomes a UNESCO day
en.origin: UNESCO's General Conference officially proclaimed 20 September the International Day of University Sport on 17 November 2015, following a proposal from the International University Sports Federation (FISU). It was celebrated for the first time in 2016. A contemporary FISU report describes an inaugural event at the University of Tehran in cooperation with the Iranian National Commission for UNESCO. FISU explains the calendar choice through the beginning of the academic year in many countries and the historical first Student World Championships in 1924. The day brings physical activity into university life and links student wellbeing with fair play and civic participation.
en.promoter: FISU proposed the international day; UNESCO Member States, assembled at the 38th General Conference, formally proclaimed it.
en.purpose: Encourage accessible university sport and its educational role in cooperation, fair play, healthy living and social engagement.
facts: The UNESCO General Conference adopted the proclamation in November 2015.
The first International Day was celebrated on 20 September 2016.
The University of Tehran hosted an inaugural celebration in 2016.

it.heading: 20 settembre: lo sport universitario diventa una giornata UNESCO
it.origin: Il 17 novembre 2015 la Conferenza generale UNESCO proclamò il 20 settembre Giornata internazionale dello sport universitario, accogliendo una proposta della Federazione internazionale dello sport universitario, FISU. La prima edizione si svolse nel 2016; una testimonianza contemporanea FISU racconta anche l'evento inaugurale all'Università di Teheran, in collaborazione con la Commissione nazionale iraniana per l'UNESCO. Secondo la federazione, il giorno coincide con l'avvio dell'anno accademico in molti Paesi e richiama i primi campionati mondiali studenteschi del 1924. La ricorrenza collega attività fisica, salute, formazione e dialogo tra studenti e università.
it.promoter: La FISU propose la giornata; gli Stati membri UNESCO la proclamarono formalmente durante la 38ª Conferenza generale.
it.purpose: Favorire lo sport accessibile negli atenei, l'inclusione, il fair play e il benessere degli studenti.
facts: La Conferenza generale UNESCO proclamò la giornata nel novembre 2015.
La prima edizione fu celebrata il 20 settembre 2016.
Nel 2016 l'Università di Teheran organizzò una celebrazione con il coinvolgimento UNESCO.

en.heading: 18–24 November: an antibiotic campaign grows into a One Health movement
en.origin: WHO's first World Antibiotic Awareness Week took place 16–22 November 2015 as part of a global action plan adopted by the World Health Assembly that year. The original campaign focused on responsible use of antibiotics and the growing threat of resistant bacteria. In 2020 the scope broadened to all antimicrobials, including antifungals, antivirals and antiparasitics, and the annual 18–24 November interval became fixed. Following inter-agency consultation, the WHO, FAO, UNEP and WOAH partnership renamed it World AMR Awareness Week in 2023. Thus its first observance was 2015, even though today's name and date range came later.
en.promoter: The World Health Organization initiated the 2015 campaign; the later Quadripartite partnership coordinates the broadened One Health framing.
en.purpose: Help professionals and the public use antimicrobial medicines appropriately while reducing the development and spread of resistant infections.
facts: The inaugural week ran from 16 to 22 November 2015.
The campaign expanded beyond antibiotics in 2020.
The four-organization Quadripartite adopted the current World AMR Awareness Week name in 2023.

it.heading: 18–24 novembre: dagli antibiotici a una campagna mondiale One Health
it.origin: L'Organizzazione mondiale della sanità organizzò la prima Settimana mondiale per la consapevolezza sugli antibiotici dal 16 al 22 novembre 2015, nell'ambito del piano globale contro la resistenza antimicrobica approvato nello stesso anno. L'iniziativa inizialmente si concentrava sugli antibiotici e sul rischio di batteri resistenti. Dal 2020 la campagna si è estesa anche agli altri antimicrobici, inclusi antivirali, antifungini e antiparassitari, stabilendo la finestra annuale del 18–24 novembre. Nel 2023 OMS, FAO, UNEP e WOAH hanno introdotto il nome World AMR Awareness Week. Non si tratta di una giornata nata nel 2023: prima edizione, ampliamento e nuova denominazione sono passaggi diversi.
it.promoter: L'OMS avviò la campagna nel 2015; successivamente le quattro organizzazioni internazionali ne hanno coordinato l'approccio One Health.
it.purpose: Promuovere un uso appropriato degli antimicrobici e prevenire la diffusione di infezioni resistenti a cure importanti.
facts: La prima campagna si svolse dal 16 al 22 novembre 2015.
Nel 2020 l'attenzione fu ampliata oltre i soli antibiotici.
Il nome attuale venne adottato dal partenariato Quadripartite nel 2023.

en.heading: 1–7 August: a global breastfeeding week begins in 1992
en.origin: The World Alliance for Breastfeeding Action, WABA, was created in 1991 to help implement the 1990 Innocenti Declaration on protecting, promoting and supporting breastfeeding. Its initial idea of a single day evolved into World Breastfeeding Week, held for the first time in 1992 and observed each 1–7 August. The first campaign grew from organized public-health advocacy rather than a United Nations General Assembly proclamation. The date range recalls the beginning of August, when the Innocenti Declaration was finalized at a WHO/UNICEF policy meeting in Florence in 1990. WABA continues to coordinate annual themes; the campaign later linked its messaging to the Sustainable Development Goals.
en.promoter: WABA originated and coordinates World Breastfeeding Week, building on the 1990 Innocenti Declaration developed by WHO/UNICEF meeting participants.
en.purpose: Support breastfeeding rights, accessible evidence-based information, and policies that make informed infant-feeding choices possible.
facts: WABA was founded in 1991 following the Innocenti Declaration of 1990.
The first World Breastfeeding Week occurred in 1992.
The annual campaign runs from 1 through 7 August and now addresses varied family and workplace issues.

it.heading: 1–7 agosto: una settimana mondiale nata nel 1992
it.origin: La World Alliance for Breastfeeding Action, WABA, nacque nel 1991 per tradurre in iniziative concrete la Dichiarazione degli Innocenti del 1990 sulla protezione e sul sostegno dell'allattamento. L'idea iniziale di una singola giornata si trasformò nella Settimana mondiale per l'allattamento, celebrata per la prima volta nel 1992 dal 1º al 7 agosto. La sua origine è un percorso di mobilitazione sanitaria, non una risoluzione istitutiva dell'Assemblea generale ONU. Il periodo richiama i giorni in cui fu definita a Firenze la dichiarazione del 1990 durante un incontro promosso da OMS e UNICEF. WABA continua a coordinare campagne e temi annuali, poi collegati anche agli Obiettivi di sviluppo sostenibile.
it.promoter: La rete WABA ideò e coordina l'iniziativa, ispirata alla Dichiarazione degli Innocenti formulata nel 1990 da partecipanti all'incontro OMS/UNICEF.
it.purpose: Sostenere informazione affidabile, diritti delle famiglie e condizioni sanitarie e lavorative favorevoli alle decisioni sull'alimentazione infantile.
facts: La WABA fu fondata nel 1991 in seguito alla Dichiarazione del 1990.
La prima Settimana mondiale per l'allattamento si svolse nel 1992.
La settimana si tiene ogni anno dall'1 al 7 agosto e propone un tema specifico.

en.heading: 28 April: from workers' remembrance to prevention at work
en.origin: The International Labour Organization began observing World Day for Safety and Health at Work on 28 April 2003 after a request from the international trade-union movement. The day built on Workers' Memorial Day, marked by unions since 1996 in memory of people killed or injured by occupational accidents and diseases. The ILO's inaugural 2003 material emphasized a preventive safety and health culture and the joint roles of governments, employers and workers. The two traditions share the calendar date but differ in emphasis: remembrance of victims and coordinated action to prevent future harm. An original ILO press account documents activities planned across countries in April 2003.
en.promoter: The International Labour Organization instituted its worldwide campaign in 2003, responding to the trade-union movement's earlier 28 April remembrance initiative.
en.purpose: Improve prevention of work-related injury and illness, encourage safer working conditions and strengthen social dialogue.
facts: International trade unions marked Workers' Memorial Day on 28 April from 1996.
ILO's first global safety-and-health day was observed on 28 April 2003.
The ILO campaign explicitly brings together workers, employers and governments.

it.heading: 28 aprile: dalla memoria dei lavoratori alla prevenzione degli infortuni
it.origin: L'Organizzazione internazionale del lavoro iniziò a celebrare il 28 aprile la Giornata mondiale per la sicurezza e la salute sul lavoro nel 2003, su richiesta del movimento sindacale internazionale. Riprendeva un'esperienza precedente: dal 1996 i sindacati ricordavano nella stessa data i lavoratori morti o feriti per incidenti e malattie professionali. La campagna OIL del 2003 pose l'accento sulla prevenzione e sulla responsabilità condivisa di governi, datori di lavoro e lavoratori. Memoria delle vittime e cultura della sicurezza sono dunque storie collegate, ma non identiche. Il materiale ufficiale dell'edizione inaugurale descrive attività e iniziative in diversi Paesi.
it.promoter: L'OIL istituì la propria campagna nel 2003 accogliendo la richiesta del mondo sindacale che celebrava già il 28 aprile.
it.purpose: Ridurre infortuni e malattie professionali attraverso prevenzione, formazione e dialogo tra le parti sociali.
facts: La commemorazione sindacale internazionale delle vittime iniziò nel 1996.
La prima giornata mondiale organizzata dall'OIL si tenne nel 2003.
La prevenzione coinvolge congiuntamente lavoratori, imprese e istituzioni.

en.heading: Third Sunday in November: a road-victims remembrance reaches the UN
en.origin: The British road-victims organization RoadPeace began a remembrance event in 1993 for people killed and injured in traffic crashes and for bereaved families. Similar initiatives spread through road-victim groups in other countries. On 26 October 2005 the United Nations General Assembly adopted resolution A/RES/60/5, inviting the world to recognize the third Sunday in November as the World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims. The UN acknowledgement did not originate the earlier civil-society tradition. The movable Sunday supports worldwide ceremonies and public discussion of preventable deaths, safe roads and support for survivors. WHO works with victims' organizations and road-safety partners to sustain the commemoration.
en.promoter: RoadPeace initiated the remembrance in 1993; the UN General Assembly formally recognized the worldwide day in 2005 through A/RES/60/5.
en.purpose: Remember those harmed by road crashes while advocating safer transport, support for victims and prevention of avoidable traffic fatalities.
facts: RoadPeace began remembrance activities in 1993 before UN recognition.
The General Assembly adopted resolution A/RES/60/5 in October 2005.
The annual date is the third Sunday in November rather than a fixed day of the month.

it.heading: Terza domenica di novembre: il ricordo delle vittime della strada arriva all'ONU
it.origin: L'associazione britannica RoadPeace iniziò nel 1993 una commemorazione delle persone morte o ferite negli incidenti stradali e delle loro famiglie. Organizzazioni analoghe diffusero l'iniziativa in altri Paesi. Il 26 ottobre 2005 l'Assemblea generale ONU adottò A/RES/60/5, invitando a riconoscere la terza domenica di novembre come Giornata mondiale in memoria delle vittime della strada. Il riconoscimento ONU non coincide con la nascita del movimento civile, precedente di dodici anni. La domenica mobile favorisce cerimonie, testimonianze e iniziative sulla sicurezza, ricordando che molti incidenti e le loro conseguenze possono essere prevenuti. L'OMS sostiene le attività insieme alle associazioni di vittime e agli operatori della sicurezza stradale.
it.promoter: RoadPeace avviò la commemorazione nel 1993; l'Assemblea generale ONU la riconobbe a livello mondiale nel 2005.
it.purpose: Ricordare vittime e familiari, promuovere strade sicure e sostenere politiche concrete contro gli incidenti evitabili.

en.heading: 5 November: UNESCO recognizes Romani language and identity
en.origin: UNESCO's General Conference proclaimed 5 November World Day of Romani Language at its 38th session in 2015. The resolution is a cultural and educational recognition intended to strengthen the preservation of the Romani language and the cultural rights of Romani-speaking communities. The observance does not create the language or its linguistic traditions: it gives institutional visibility to a heritage that existed long before UNESCO. The agency highlights dialectal diversity, research and the importance of teaching and sharing the language across generations. The individual year of a first UNESCO-organized annual ceremony and the exact historical reason for choosing 5 November are not established by the documents reviewed, so neither is invented.
en.promoter: UNESCO's Member States proclaimed the international day in 2015; its purpose reflects advocacy for Romani-language preservation, without assigning an unverified individual founder.
en.purpose: Support linguistic diversity, access to education, cultural recognition and the transmission of Romani heritage.
facts: UNESCO proclaimed the observance during its 38th General Conference in 2015.
The calendar date is 5 November, with no first annual event verified here.
The observance specifically concerns language preservation and intercultural understanding.

it.heading: 5 novembre: l'UNESCO riconosce lingua e identità romaní
it.origin: La Conferenza generale UNESCO proclamò il 5 novembre Giornata mondiale della lingua romaní nel 2015, durante la sua 38ª sessione. Si tratta di un riconoscimento culturale ed educativo destinato a sostenere la lingua e i diritti delle comunità che la parlano. La proclamazione non ha creato la lingua né le sue tradizioni, che sono naturalmente molto precedenti. L'UNESCO richiama l'importanza dei diversi dialetti, dello studio linguistico e della trasmissione fra generazioni. Le fonti istituzionali utilizzate non individuano in modo indipendente né la prima cerimonia annuale organizzata sotto la nuova proclamazione né il motivo storico esatto della scelta del 5 novembre: questi dati restano aperti.
it.promoter: Gli Stati membri riuniti nella Conferenza generale UNESCO adottarono il riconoscimento nel 2015, senza individuare un singolo fondatore personale verificato.
it.purpose: Difendere il pluralismo linguistico, l'educazione e la continuità della cultura e del patrimonio romaní.
facts: La proclamazione UNESCO avvenne alla 38ª Conferenza generale del 2015.

en.heading: 24–30 April: regional vaccination campaigns become one global WHO week
en.origin: In April 2012 the World Health Organization organized World Immunization Week as a worldwide coordinated campaign following earlier vaccination weeks in several of its regions. The WHO's own first global 2012 campaign page documents the transition to a common international awareness initiative, with activities linked to the protection vaccines provide against infectious diseases. Its date range is now generally 24–30 April, although some 2012 materials use the slightly different 21–28 April period. It should not be misrepresented as an observance founded by a specific UN General Assembly resolution. The WHO campaign emphasizes reaching underserved communities, maintaining vaccination systems and protecting people throughout life.
en.promoter: The World Health Organization coordinated the first global World Immunization Week in 2012, building on previous regional immunization campaigns.
en.purpose: Promote evidence-based vaccination, equitable access to immunization and protection from preventable infectious diseases.
facts: WHO's first global campaign is recorded in April 2012.
Its annual modern campaign interval is 24–30 April.

it.heading: 24–30 aprile: le campagne vaccinali regionali diventano una settimana globale OMS
it.origin: Nel 2012 l'Organizzazione mondiale della sanità avviò una Settimana mondiale dell'immunizzazione coordinata su scala globale, facendo convergere campagne vaccinali già esistenti in varie regioni. La pagina ufficiale della prima edizione documenta l'obiettivo di sensibilizzare sull'importanza delle vaccinazioni contro le malattie infettive. Oggi il calendario indica generalmente il 24–30 aprile, mentre alcuni materiali della prima edizione riportavano una finestra leggermente diversa, dal 21 al 28 aprile. Non si attribuisce quindi l'origine a una inesistente risoluzione istitutiva dell'Assemblea generale. L'OMS insiste su accesso equo, comunità meno servite e continuità dei programmi vaccinali.

en.heading: 23 March: the birthday of a worldwide weather cooperation system
en.origin: The World Meteorological Organization's Executive Committee adopted Resolution 6 (EC-XII) in 1960, establishing an annual World Meteorological Day for 23 March. The day recalls 23 March 1950, when the convention establishing the WMO entered into force, not the year the annual celebration began. An institutional WMO retrospective confirms that the first World Meteorological Day took place on 23 March 1961, with more than sixty countries reporting activities. The WMO grew out of international scientific cooperation in sharing weather observations and forecasts; annual observances now explore climate services, water resources, severe-weather alerts and meteorological research.
en.promoter: The WMO Executive Committee selected the annual date in Resolution 6 (EC-XII) in 1960; no single personal founder is attributed.
en.purpose: Explain how cross-border meteorological research, forecasting and early warning systems protect communities and livelihoods.

it.heading: 23 marzo: la nascita di un sistema mondiale di cooperazione meteorologica
it.origin: Nel 1960 il Comitato esecutivo dell'Organizzazione meteorologica mondiale adottò la Risoluzione 6 (EC-XII), individuando il 23 marzo per la celebrazione annuale della meteorologia. La data ricorda il 23 marzo 1950, giorno di entrata in vigore della Convenzione istitutiva dell'OMM, non l'anno della prima ricorrenza. Una retrospettiva istituzionale documenta la prima Giornata meteorologica mondiale il 23 marzo 1961, con iniziative segnalate in oltre sessanta Paesi. Da allora la collaborazione scientifica fra servizi nazionali ha assunto un ruolo centrale nel monitoraggio del tempo, del clima e delle risorse idriche e nella diffusione di allerte tempestive.

en.heading: Last Thursday of September: the IMO brings shipping into public view
en.origin: World Maritime Day was conceived by the International Maritime Organization in 1978 as a way to explain its work to member governments and the wider maritime community. An IMO Secretary-General's historical speech describes this origin and the intention to organize activities around a yearly maritime theme. Today the international observance takes place on the last Thursday of September, while national and parallel events may be scheduled on other dates. The IMO uses the day to discuss safer shipping, the rights and skills of seafarers, preventing pollution by ships and implementation of international rules. It is an institutional campaign launched in 1978, not a commemoration attributed to a single seafarer or an invented General Assembly founding act.
en.promoter: The International Maritime Organization established the international observance in 1978, with its Council choosing annual themes.
en.purpose: Increase understanding of the maritime sector and cooperation on safety, environmental protection and effective shipping standards.
facts: The IMO dates the conception of World Maritime Day to 1978.
The global observance is held on the final Thursday in September.
The IMO Council identifies a theme reflecting the organization's maritime priorities.

it.heading: Ultimo giovedì di settembre: l'IMO racconta la navigazione al mondo
it.origin: La Giornata mondiale del mare e del trasporto marittimo fu concepita dall'Organizzazione marittima internazionale nel 1978 per far conoscere il proprio lavoro ai governi aderenti e alla comunità marittima. Un discorso storico del Segretario generale IMO ne ricostruisce l'origine e spiega l'intenzione di organizzare iniziative attorno a un tema diverso ogni anno. Oggi la celebrazione internazionale cade l'ultimo giovedì di settembre, mentre gli eventi nazionali o paralleli possono seguire altri calendari. L'IMO affronta sicurezza delle navi, competenze degli equipaggi, prevenzione dell'inquinamento e applicazione delle convenzioni. È una campagna istituzionale avviata nel 1978, non il ricordo di un singolo navigatore.

it.purpose: Rendere visibile l'importanza della navigazione e della cooperazione internazionale per sicurezza, sostenibilità e norme marittime.

en.heading: Third Thursday in November: from UNESCO philosophy meetings to a world day
en.origin: UNESCO first organized Philosophy Day activities in 2002, and in 2005 its General Conference formally established World Philosophy Day on the third Thursday in November. Institutional documentation stresses the value of philosophical reflection for questioning assumptions, developing independent judgment and promoting dialogue across cultures. The year of the first activities and the year of formal proclamation must therefore be recorded separately: 2002 is not a 2005 General Conference vote. The movable Thursday also means the date changes each November. Conferences, classroom debates and public philosophy events make the discipline accessible beyond universities, with a particular emphasis on young people.
en.promoter: UNESCO organized philosophy events from 2002; the UNESCO General Conference institutionalized the worldwide day in 2005.
en.purpose: Encourage critical and independent thought, philosophical education, cultural dialogue and public reflection.
facts: UNESCO organized philosophy-day events as early as 2002.

it.heading: Terzo giovedì di novembre: dagli incontri UNESCO a una giornata mondiale
it.origin: L'UNESCO iniziò a organizzare attività dedicate alla filosofia nel 2002; nel 2005 la Conferenza generale proclamò formalmente la Giornata mondiale della filosofia, da celebrare il terzo giovedì di novembre. I documenti istituzionali ne sottolineano il valore per il ragionamento critico, l'autonomia di giudizio e il confronto tra culture. È importante distinguere l'avvio delle manifestazioni dalla successiva istituzione ufficiale: il 2002 non è la data della risoluzione del 2005. Trattandosi di un giovedì mobile, il giorno del mese cambia ogni anno. Conferenze, incontri pubblici e dibattiti scolastici rendono la filosofia uno strumento di partecipazione, specialmente per i giovani.

en.heading: 2 May: Poland makes room for its white-and-red flag
en.origin: Poland's Sejm established the Day of the Flag of the Republic of Poland through an amendment to legislation on the national emblem, colours and anthem adopted on 20 February 2004. It is observed every 2 May, between Labour Day on 1 May and Constitution Day on 3 May. Government heritage material links the date to Polish flags raised in Berlin on 2 May 1945 and to the history of the flag during the communist period. The modern commemorative day must be separated from older recognition of Poland's white-and-red colours in 1831 and the later regulation of the national flag in 1919. The day promotes respectful display and knowledge of state symbols; it is not necessarily a general day off work.
en.promoter: The Polish Sejm established the observance by a statutory amendment in February 2004; no unsupported single personal proposer is attributed.
en.purpose: Promote knowledge of Poland's flag, national symbols and the historical changes in their public use.
facts: The Sejm enacted the 2 May Flag Day through legislation in 2004.
Polish white-and-red national colours were regulated long before the modern holiday.
The date sits between Labour Day and Constitution Day and commemorates a 1945 Berlin flag episode.

it.heading: 2 maggio: la Polonia dedica una giornata alla bandiera bianca e rossa
it.origin: Il Sejm, il Parlamento polacco, istituì il Giorno della bandiera della Repubblica di Polonia mediante una modifica della legge su stemma, colori e inno nazionale approvata il 20 febbraio 2004. Si celebra il 2 maggio, tra la Festa del lavoro del 1º maggio e quella della Costituzione del 3 maggio. Il Ministero della cultura collega la data alle bandiere polacche issate a Berlino il 2 maggio 1945 e alla storia dei simboli durante il periodo comunista. La ricorrenza moderna va distinta dal riconoscimento dei colori nazionali nel 1831 e dalla disciplina della bandiera del 1919. La giornata promuove rispetto per i simboli e conoscenza della loro storia, senza essere necessariamente un giorno festivo non lavorativo.

it.purpose: Promuovere conoscenza e rispetto dei simboli polacchi e della loro evoluzione storica.

en.heading: 27 June: Canada declares a day to recognize cultural diversity
en.origin: On 13 November 2002 the Government of Canada designated 27 June Canadian Multiculturalism Day by Royal Proclamation. This official celebration was introduced long after the federal multiculturalism policy announced in 1971, and after the 1988 Canadian Multiculturalism Act: those milestones are precursors, not the day’s founding proclamation. The date falls within the country's broader June-to-July Celebrate Canada period and offers space to appreciate many cultural communities and to discuss discrimination, inclusion and shared civic life. Government material identifies the 2002 designation but does not establish why 27 June rather than another day was chosen, nor the first specific ceremonial event, so those details remain unverified.
en.promoter: The Government of Canada established the day by Royal Proclamation in 2002; the multiculturalism legislation and policy are earlier, distinct milestones.
en.purpose: Recognize cultural diversity and encourage equal opportunities, community participation and action against discrimination.
facts: Canada announced its federal multiculturalism policy in 1971.
The Canadian Multiculturalism Act became law in 1988.

it.heading: 27 giugno: il Canada istituisce una giornata per il pluralismo culturale
it.origin: Il 13 novembre 2002 il Governo canadese designò il 27 giugno Giornata del multiculturalismo canadese mediante una proclamazione reale. La celebrazione ufficiale arrivò dopo la politica federale sul multiculturalismo annunciata nel 1971 e dopo il Canadian Multiculturalism Act del 1988: sono tappe precedenti, non la proclamazione istitutiva della giornata. Il 27 giugno si inserisce nel periodo di celebrazioni civiche Celebrate Canada e offre occasione per riconoscere il contributo delle diverse comunità e discutere inclusione e discriminazioni. Le fonti governative confermano la data di istituzione del 2002, ma non dimostrano perché sia stato scelto proprio il 27 giugno né quale sia stata la prima specifica cerimonia annuale.

it.purpose: Valorizzare la diversità culturale, promuovere pari opportunità e incoraggiare la partecipazione delle comunità.
facts: La politica canadese sul multiculturalismo fu annunciata nel 1971.

es.heading: 27 de junio: Canadá celebra su diversidad cultural
es.origin: El Gobierno de Canadá designó el 27 de junio como Día del Multiculturalismo Canadiense el 13 de noviembre de 2002. La decisión llegó después de dos hitos diferentes: la política federal de multiculturalismo anunciada en 1971 y la Ley de Multiculturalismo Canadiense de 1988. Ninguno de esos antecedentes debe confundirse con la creación de la conmemoración anual. El día forma parte del periodo cívico Celebrate Canada y reconoce la contribución de comunidades de distintas procedencias, al tiempo que invita a reflexionar sobre la inclusión y la discriminación. Las fuentes gubernamentales consultadas confirman la designación de 2002, pero no explican por qué se eligió exactamente el 27 de junio ni documentan una primera ceremonia.

fr.heading: 27 juin : le Canada célèbre la diversité culturelle
fr.origin: Le gouvernement du Canada a désigné le 27 juin Journée canadienne du multiculturalisme le 13 novembre 2002. Cette décision est postérieure à deux étapes distinctes : l'annonce d'une politique fédérale du multiculturalisme en 1971 et l'adoption de la Loi sur le multiculturalisme canadien en 1988. Ces précédents ne constituent pas l'acte de création de la journée annuelle. Inscrite dans la période de célébrations de la fête du Canada, elle met en valeur les communautés de diverses origines et encourage la réflexion sur l'inclusion, la discrimination et la vie civique commune. Les sources gouvernementales confirment la désignation de 2002, sans démontrer pourquoi le 27 juin a été retenu ni dater une première cérémonie.

de.heading: 27. Juni: Kanada würdigt seine kulturelle Vielfalt
de.origin: Die kanadische Regierung bestimmte am 13. November 2002 den 27. Juni zum jährlichen Tag des kanadischen Multikulturalismus. Dies geschah nach zwei früheren Meilensteinen: der 1971 verkündeten Bundespolitik des Multikulturalismus und dem Multiculturalism Act von 1988. Sie bietet auch Anlass, über gesellschaftliche Teilhabe, Diskriminierung und Chancengleichheit nachzudenken. Die Regierungsquellen belegen die Benennung im Jahr 2002, geben aber keinen gesicherten Grund für die Wahl des 27. Juni und keine nachweisbare erste Einzelveranstaltung an.

en.heading: 28 February: India remembers the Raman effect through science education
en.origin: India designated 28 February National Science Day in 1986 after the National Council for Science and Technology Communication requested recognition from the government. The first official National Science Day followed on 28 February 1987. The date commemorates the announcement of the Raman effect on 28 February 1928, when physicist C. V. Raman presented the discovery concerning light scattering. Raman later received the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics. The experiment, the government designation and the first public commemoration are three different events. Indian schools, universities and research institutes use the anniversary to share scientific discoveries and encourage critical inquiry.
en.promoter: The National Council for Science and Technology Communication proposed the date in 1986 and the Indian government accepted it.
en.purpose: Encourage science education, research literacy and interest in scientific careers and discoveries.

en.heading: 25 January: India's election body welcomes new voters
en.origin: In 2011 the Election Commission of India created National Voters' Day to be observed each 25 January, the anniversary of the Commission's establishment on 25 January 1950. The awareness day therefore began more than six decades after the founding of the institution it commemorates. Its activities focus on registration, knowledge of voting rights and participation, particularly for citizens reaching voting age. The Election Commission's own reports describe ceremonies at polling stations and at district, state and national levels, including the distribution of voter identity cards. The observance is an outreach campaign initiated by the electoral authority rather than a new election law.
en.promoter: The Election Commission of India instituted the annual event in 2011 to mark its own foundation date.
en.purpose: Increase informed electoral participation, voter registration and civic awareness, especially among younger eligible citizens.

en.heading: 1 July: from Confederation celebrations to the modern Canada Day
en.origin: Canada's 1 July commemoration celebrates Confederation, formed on 1 July 1867 under the British North America Act. Governor General Lord Monck issued a proclamation on 20 June 1868 encouraging celebrations the following 1 July, making 1868 the earliest official civic anniversary identified here. These dates must remain separate rather than incorrectly describing the holiday as having first begun in 1982.

en.heading: Third Monday in January: the long campaign for a Martin Luther King Jr. holiday

it.origin: Il presidente Ronald Reagan firmò la legge federale 98-144 il 2 novembre 1983, istituendo il terzo lunedì di gennaio come festività nazionale dedicata a Martin Luther King Jr. La prima celebrazione federale in tutti gli Stati Uniti si svolse il 20 gennaio 1986. La legge arrivò dopo una lunga mobilitazione iniziata poco dopo l'assassinio di King nell'aprile 1968. Il deputato John Conyers presentò un primo progetto di legge nei giorni successivi alla morte; in seguito la deputata Katie Hall contribuì all'approvazione della proposta alla Camera. Il terzo lunedì sostituì la data fissa del 15 gennaio per ridurre le interruzioni delle attività governative. Un'altra legge del 1994 favorì la commemorazione attraverso il servizio alla comunità.

en.heading: 14 April: Poland establishes a modern holiday for a medieval baptism
en.origin: Poland's Sejm enacted a law on 22 February 2019 creating the Baptism of Poland Day on 14 April, with legal effect from publication on 9 April 2019. The day recalls the baptism of ruler Mieszko I in 966, an event widely treated as a symbolic beginning of Polish statehood and Poland's connection to Latin Christianity. The chosen date of 14 April reflects the traditional hypothesis that the ceremony took place on Holy Saturday in 966. The Polish government's historical account explicitly cautions that neither the exact day nor the site of the baptism is established with certainty. The modern statutory holiday is distinct from the medieval ceremony and from earlier jubilee observances; a first separately documented annual celebration under the 2019 law is not asserted.

en.heading: 1 October: coffee growers and consumers get a shared international date
en.origin: In March 2014 the International Coffee Council, acting through the International Coffee Organization (ICO), agreed to establish an annual International Coffee Day on 1 October. The first international event took place on 1 October 2015 during the ICO Council session and the first Global Coffee Forum at Expo Milano, bringing together producing and consuming countries. An ICO announcement records the participation of member states and coffee associations, with goals including recognizing growers, workers and sustainable production.

en.heading: Starting 25 May: the UN links decolonization to a week of solidarity
en.origin: The United Nations General Assembly called for an annual Week of Solidarity with the Peoples of Non-Self-Governing Territories in resolution A/RES/54/91, adopted on 6 December 1999. The week begins on 25 May and highlights the continuing obligations of administering powers toward peoples who have not achieved full self-government. Its political background is the United Nations Charter and the Declaration on the Granting of Independence to Colonial Countries and Peoples of 1960. The General Assembly's decision asked for support in safeguarding natural resources, property rights and access to political participation. The founding act was adopted after May 1999; the institutional evidence consulted does not independently establish a first actual annual week, so its year is left unknown rather than retroactively assigned to an earlier date.

en.heading: From an April 2006 bird-conservation campaign to two migration dates
en.origin: The secretariats of the African-Eurasian Migratory Waterbird Agreement (AEWA) and the Convention on Migratory Species (CMS) launched the first World Migratory Bird Day on 8–9 April 2006. en.heading: Late June: Britain's Armed Forces Day begins with Chatham in 2009

The national event rotates between cities, and the annual public campaign falls on a Saturday in late June.

en.heading: 9 April: Canada gives the Battle of Vimy Ridge a national remembrance day
en.origin: On 3 April 2003 Canada's government officially designated 9 April as a national day of remembrance for the Battle of Vimy Ridge, the 1917 First World War engagement in northern France. The battle began on 9 April 1917, giving the modern observance its historical calendar date. Veterans Affairs Canada documents the 2003 designation, and a message from the Governor General ten years later recalls that Canadians had gathered each 9 April since 2003 to honour the battle. About 3,600 Canadians died during the operation and more than 7,000 were wounded. The 2003 commemorative decision is distinct from the event of 1917 and the later centenary ceremonies in 2017.

en.heading: 25 April: the first Anzac Day remembers Gallipoli in 1916

After the war public ceremonies became more standardized. en.heading: 25 April: New Zealand's original Anzac Day was a half-holiday in 1916

en.heading: 19 March: France legally commemorates the Algerian War ceasefire
en.origin: French Law No. 2012-1361 of 6 December 2012 established 19 March as a national day of remembrance for civilian and military victims of the Algerian War and of fighting in Tunisia and Morocco. The chosen date recalls the ceasefire in Algeria on 19 March 1962 after the Évian agreements. The legislative record traces a long process, including proposals first advanced in the early 2000s and Constitutional Council review in November 2012. The date's role in the contested memory of decolonization must not be confused with a legal claim that every victim died before the ceasefire. en.heading: 26 January: Italy establishes remembrance of the Alpini and Nikolajewka
en.origin: Italy's Law No. 44 of 5 May 2022 formally recognizes 26 January each year as the National Day of Remembrance and Sacrifice of the Alpini. en.heading: 11 November: France turns the 1918 armistice into a national holiday
en.origin: France's Parliament enacted the law of 24 October 1922 establishing 11 November as the annual public holiday commemorating victory and peace following the First World War. The selected date recalls the armistice signed on 11 November 1918, which brought fighting on the Western Front to an end. Public remembrance had already developed after the war, including a 1920 tribute to an unknown soldier, so the 1922 statute is not the original beginning of all remembrance. A separate law of 28 February 2012 expanded the annual homage to include all those who died for France, without replacing other national remembrance days. Parliamentary records independently establish the legal origins but do not identify one single inaugural 1922 ceremony as the first French memorial, so that year remains unverified.

en.heading: 25 April: UNESCO dedicates a day to small island developing states
en.origin: UNESCO proclaimed 25 April the International Day for Small Island Developing States in 2025 through its General Conference. The annual date recalls the first global conference on small island developing states, held in Barbados in 1994, rather than the year UNESCO adopted the day. The new recognition focuses on the distinctive strengths and vulnerabilities of island societies: ocean knowledge, cultural heritage, education, freshwater resources, and the threats associated with climate change and coastal damage. UNESCO's 2023–2029 operational strategy for small island developing states already set out six accelerator programmes. That strategy preceded the commemorative decision and is not itself the establishing instrument. en.heading: From 21 March: a UN week calls for solidarity against racism
en.origin: The UN General Assembly adopted resolution A/RES/34/24 on 15 November 1979, calling for a Week of Solidarity with the Peoples Struggling against Racism and Racial Discrimination, starting annually on 21 March. Its programme called on states to educate the public, involve young people, protect migrants and oppose organizations propagating racial hatred. The 21 March opening coincides with the separate International Day for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination, established after the police killings at Sharpeville, South Africa, on 21 March 1960. The 1979 week followed that earlier single-day commemoration; it did not create or replace it. The original mandate prescribes an annual week but does not establish a specific first ceremony and the first observed year remains unasserted.

en.heading: 10 December: Sweden's flag-day recognition of Alfred Nobel
en.origin: Sweden's ordinance on official flag days, Regulation (1982:270), expressly includes 10 December as Nobeldagen, Nobel Day. The official online text is the consolidated version updated through 2023, so its presence does not by itself prove in which year 10 December first entered the regulation. The day is linked to Alfred Nobel's death on 10 December 1896 and to the Nobel Prize award ceremonies, first held in Stockholm in 1901. These are distinct events: Nobel's death is the calendar rationale, the first prize ceremony precedes the current regulation, and the Swedish flag-day listing establishes contemporary civic status. en.heading: 30 November: the Philippines honours revolutionary Andrés Bonifacio by law
en.origin: Philippine Act No. 2946, approved on 16 February 1921, amended the Administrative Code to make 30 November of each year a legal holiday. The National Museum of the Philippines identifies the date as the birth anniversary of Andrés Bonifacio, born on 30 November 1863, a key figure in the struggle against Spanish colonial rule. The act's original text and Senate legislative register establish the legal founding milestone; the museum provides the historical connection to Bonifacio's role in the Katipunan revolutionary organization. The designation is not the date of the Philippine Revolution itself, and the law does not independently document the first annual public ceremony after approval. Accordingly the first observed year is left unknown rather than assumed to be 1921.

it.heading: 30 novembre: le Filippine ricordano per legge il rivoluzionario Andrés Bonifacio

Il Museo nazionale delle Filippine collega la data all'anniversario della nascita di Andrés Bonifacio, avvenuta il 30 novembre 1863, figura centrale della lotta contro il dominio coloniale spagnolo. Il testo originale della legge e il registro del Senato provano il passaggio giuridico; il Museo documenta il legame storico con la società rivoluzionaria Katipunan. Il giorno scelto non coincide con l'avvio della rivoluzione filippina e la legge non dimostra autonomamente la prima cerimonia annuale dopo l'adozione. L'anno della prima celebrazione ufficiale rimane quindi sconosciuto, senza dedurlo dal 1921.

en.heading: 16 November: Portugal marks the sea and the law governing it
en.origin: Portugal's National Sea Day was established in 1998, the year of Lisbon's Expo devoted to oceans and of the International Year of the Ocean. The Portuguese government's own account confirms that the 16 November date recalls the entry into force of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on 16 November 1994. The historical legal entry into force in 1994 and the later Portuguese national day created in 1998 are distinct. en.heading: 10 October: Finland's literary flag day grew through three historical stages
en.origin: Finland marks 10 October as Aleksis Kivi Day and Finnish Literature Day, recalling the birthday of novelist Aleksis Kivi, born in 1834 and author of Seven Brothers, published in 1870. The University of Helsinki Almanac Office documents the celebration's gradual recognition: the Aleksi name day was associated with Kivi from 1929, the day became a separate commemorative entry in 1950, and it was marked on flag-day lists from 1953. A flagging decree of 1978 added the description Finnish Literature Day to the existing observance. Accordingly 1950 is the earlier individually documented memorial, while 1978 recognizes the present combined literary-day title. Its customary flag-day status must not be confused with a statutory paid public holiday.

en.heading: 11 December: Canada flags a constitutional autonomy milestone
en.origin: Canada's federal commemoration of the Statute of Westminster takes place each 11 December, on the anniversary of the British statute enacted on 11 December 1931. The Act followed the Imperial Conferences of 1926 and 1930, and recognized the legislative autonomy of self-governing dominions including Canada. Canadian Heritage explains that, where two flagpoles are available, federal buildings may fly the Royal Union Flag beside Canada's National Flag, with the Canadian flag taking precedence. The government's explanation describes the modern annual remembrance, while the Department of Justice reproduces the statute's original text. The Act of 1931 is the historical event being commemorated, not necessarily the legal instrument that created the later Canadian flag-day observance. No first formal proclamation or first annual flag ceremony has been individually sourced, so both fields remain unknown.

en.heading: 5 April: Korea's Arbor Day shifts from public holiday to civic campaign
en.origin: South Korea's Arbor Day on 5 April is linked to a longer history of national tree-planting initiatives. The Korean Ministry of the Interior notes that a 1910 tree-planting ceremony under the Korean Empire preceded the modern observance; during Japanese rule, a different Arbor Day date, 3 April, was also used. A presidential decree on 4 June 1949 made 5 April a statutory public holiday. The day was temporarily changed in 1960 and restored to 5 April in 1961, then included as a statutory commemoration in 1982. From June 2005 the date ceased to be a general public holiday while remaining a commemorative day. These shifts show why the modern date and civic status cannot be described as unchanged since 1910.

A first actual ceremony under the 2019 national statute is not established in the institutional chronology and is left unknown.

en.heading: Third Monday in May: Korea's coming-of-age tradition becomes a modern public day
en.origin: South Korea's Coming of Age Day celebrates the responsibilities and civic standing of people entering adulthood. The Ministry of the Interior traces the much older Korean coming-of-age tradition to historical court records, including a Goryeo ceremony in 965. The modern statutory commemorative day was designated on 30 March 1973, originally falling on 20 April. The government changed it to 6 May in 1975 and to the third Monday in May in September 1984, establishing today's movable schedule. These shifts explain why the date is not a fixed traditional birthday or an unchanged medieval anniversary. The 1973 statutory recognition is distinct from earlier family and court coming-of-age ceremonies. No independently verified inaugural modern government ceremony is claimed.

it.heading: Terzo lunedì di maggio: un'antica tradizione coreana diventa giornata pubblica moderna

en.heading: 5 May: Korean Children's Day predates the current statutory holiday
en.origin: Children's Day in Korea originated in the early twentieth-century children's rights movement led by Bang Jeong-hwan and youth groups. A primary 1923 newspaper source, preserved by the Korean History Institute, calls for recognition and respect for children, documenting the first commemorative activities around 1 May 1923. After liberation, South Korean organizers resumed celebrations on 5 May in 1946. The government designated 5 May as Children's Day in the Child Welfare Act of 30 December 1961, listed it among statutory commemorations in 1973 and made it a statutory public holiday in January 1975. The original 1923 campaign, 1961 legal date and 1975 holiday status are distinct. No 1923 event should be presented as already having taken place on the modern 5 May date.

en.heading: 8 October: Peru commemorates Miguel Grau and the naval battle of Angamos
en.origin: Peru remembers the naval Battle of Angamos, fought on 8 October 1879 during the War of the Pacific, when Admiral Miguel Grau was killed aboard the monitor Huáscar. The date also became part of the national Navy Day tradition. The Peruvian Congress' historical legal account identifies Law 9126 of 3 June 1940, which formally declared 8 October a national tribute to Grau and his companions and dedicated it to the flag oath of naval cadets. It followed an earlier 1921 law that already tied Navy Day to the naval battle, while further changes to Navy Day's own calendar followed in 1945. The 1940 tribute and the 1879 battle are distinct; the first actual ceremony under the 1940 commemorative act is not independently documented in the original sources, and remains unknown.

en.heading: 7 June: Peru distinguishes the Battle of Arica and modern Flag Day law
en.origin: Peru's Law 31788, published on 15 June 2023 after approval by Congress, made 7 June a national paid holiday commemorating both the Battle of Arica and Flag Day. The legislation amended Legislative Decree 713 on annual holidays and required public institutions to renew the oath of fidelity to the Peruvian flag. The date recalls the Battle of Arica of 7 June 1880 during the War of the Pacific, a historical event remembered long before the new nationwide non-working holiday. en.heading: 9 December: Peru legislates remembrance before making Ayacucho a holiday

en.heading: 22 September: UNESCO recognizes the living heritage of nomadic communities
en.origin: On 6 November 2025 UNESCO's 43rd General Conference, meeting in Samarkand, adopted the proclamation of 22 September as International Day of Nomadic Heritage under agenda document 43 C/51. Kyrgyzstan initiated the proposal, with Kazakhstan among its co-sponsors, as confirmed by governmental accounts of the conference. Kazakhstan's foreign ministry explains that 22 September was associated with the autumn equinox, symbolizing harmony between people and nature. The day seeks greater recognition of pastoralist knowledge, seasonal migration, traditional crafts and intergenerational teaching, without implying nomadic ways of life began with UNESCO's declaration. Separate UNESCO intangible-heritage decisions have already recognized practices such as Mongol nomad migration. The proclamation followed September 2025, and no first annual observance in September 2026 is individually evidenced by the consulted original documents; the inaugural-year field remains unknown.

en.heading: 9 April: the Philippines remembers Bataan with a statutory Day of Valor
en.origin: The Philippines' Republic Act No. 3022, approved on 6 April 1961, proclaimed 9 April Bataan Day and established it as a legal holiday in memory of the soldiers and civilians who defended the Bataan Peninsula during the Second World War. The date recalls the surrender of forces on Bataan on 9 April 1942, preceding the brutal Bataan Death March. Article 1 of the 1961 statute explicitly asks people to observe one minute of silence at 4:30 in the afternoon. The 1961 founding law, 1942 military event and 1987 name are distinct; the source does not independently prove the first official public ceremony after adoption.

en.heading: 12 October: Italy creates a modern Christopher Columbus observance in 2004
en.origin: An Italian Prime Minister's Directive dated 20 February 2004 designated 12 October every year as National Christopher Columbus Day. The directive was proposed by the Minister for Italians Abroad, Mirko Tremaglia, and signed by Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi. It instructed public administrations to support initiatives about the historical voyage that reached the Americas on 12 October 1492. The act also created an honorary committee to coordinate activities, and the Italian Presidency's records show that President Carlo Azeglio Ciampi received the committee on 5 October 2004, when the official logo was presented. The historical landfall in 1492, the 2004 formal decree and that October preparatory event are separate; the latter does not independently prove the first full annual ceremony on 12 October. The voyage is an appropriate topic for considering both transatlantic contacts and the grave consequences of European colonization for Indigenous peoples.

en.heading: Second Monday in October: Columbus Day becomes a United States federal holiday
en.origin: The United States Congress first adopted a joint resolution on 30 April 1934 requesting annual presidential Columbus Day proclamations, reflecting older community celebrations associated with Italian-American heritage. The federal holiday itself was created in the Uniform Monday Holiday Act of 1968 and took effect in 1971, placing the observance on the second Monday of October rather than always 12 October, the date associated with Columbus's 1492 landfall in the Caribbean. The National Archives distinguishes the 1934 proclamation requirement from the 1968 federal holiday law and its actual start in 1971. Archived White House proclamations show presidents continuing the annual ceremony under 36 U.S.C. 107. The historical legacy is contested: the voyage also opened an era of European conquest, forced displacement and violence against Indigenous peoples. That complex history should be part of educational context without falsely suggesting Congress had enacted a federal holiday in 1934.
en.promoter: The US Congress established the federal public holiday through the Uniform Monday Holiday Act in 1968; an earlier 1934 congressional resolution requested presidential proclamations.
en.purpose: Examine the historical legacy of transatlantic contact and its continuing interpretations, including Italian-American heritage and the effects on Indigenous societies.

it.heading: Secondo lunedì di ottobre: negli USA il Columbus Day diventa festa federale
it.origin: Negli Stati Uniti il Congresso adottò il 30 aprile 1934 una risoluzione con cui invitava il Presidente a proclamare annualmente il Columbus Day, riprendendo celebrazioni comunitarie già esistenti, specialmente fra gli italoamericani. Il giorno festivo federale vero e proprio fu invece introdotto dall'Uniform Monday Holiday Act del 1968, entrato in vigore nel 1971: per questo la festa cade il secondo lunedì di ottobre e non sempre il 12 ottobre, data tradizionalmente collegata allo sbarco di Colombo nei Caraibi nel 1492. Gli Archivi nazionali distinguono la richiesta di proclamazioni del 1934 dalla legge federale del 1968 e dall'applicazione del 1971. I proclami presidenziali conservati nell'archivio della Casa Bianca mostrano la continuità delle celebrazioni. La storia è oggetto di discussione perché il viaggio aprì anche una fase di conquista europea, spostamenti forzati e violenze contro i popoli indigeni. Questo contesto non va ignorato né confuso con l'istituzione della festa.
it.promoter: Il Congresso degli Stati Uniti introdusse la festività federale con la legge del 1968, dopo una precedente risoluzione del 1934 sui proclami presidenziali.
it.purpose: Conoscere la storia dei contatti atlantici e le differenti interpretazioni del loro impatto, dalla cultura italoamericana alle conseguenze per le popolazioni indigene.
facts: Nel 1934 una risoluzione richiese proclami presidenziali annuali.

en.heading: 24 April: Canada's parliamentary recognition of Armenian genocide remembrance
en.origin: On 24 April 2015 the Canadian House of Commons adopted Motion M-587, moved by MP Brad Butt. It reaffirmed the House's earlier Armenian-genocide recognition resolution of 21 April 2004, recognized April as Genocide Remembrance, Condemnation and Prevention Month and expressly identified 24 April as Armenian Genocide Memorial Day. The date recalls the arrests of Armenian intellectuals in Constantinople on 24 April 1915, explained in a contemporary statement by the Armenian ambassador in Ottawa. The 2004 genocide recognition and 2015 explicit parliamentary memorial-day acknowledgment are separate milestones, and the 2015 motion is not itself an act establishing a nationwide statutory day off. A first community observance in Canada predating Parliament's acknowledgment cannot be fixed from those records.

La data ricorda gli arresti di intellettuali armeni a Costantinopoli il 24 aprile 1915, richiamati anche in una dichiarazione dell'ambasciatore armeno a Ottawa. Il riconoscimento del genocidio nel 2004 e la menzione parlamentare della ricorrenza nel 2015 sono due passaggi distinti.
